finding: reconcile chained with `?` after the terminal workflow_runs UPDATE already committed → a transient task-list DB error wrongly fails the run-terminal transition; a retry then hits rows_affected=0 and skips reconcile, leaking until the boot sweep.

terminal status write + reconcile are two separate autocommit statements (also in cancel_cas): a reconcile error after the status commit leaves the run terminal with open rows (INV-1 transiently violated) until the boot sweep. Same root as the correctness partial-success finding.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 (non-fatal reconcile; boot sweep is the documented backstop)

finding: cancel_cas propagates a reconcile failure via `?` after the cancel already committed → surfaces a landed user-cancel as an error.

status_schema() advertises only pending/in_progress/completed, but TaskItemCreate/Patch deserialize Option<TaskStatus>, which now accepts "abandoned" — a model could set the system-only Abandoned state, contradicting DEC-2's stated invariant.
the crash-recovery INV-3 leg calls reconcile_orphaned_task_lists directly, never through sweep_at_boot — deleting the production wiring in sweep_at_boot would leave every test green.
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 (added sweep_at_boot_reconciles_orphaned_task_rows driving the real boot entry point)

finding: the dedicated INV-2 test (all-completed run) is non-discriminating: it passes even if the reconcile hook is deleted (no open rows to reconcile).
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 (TEST-2 now includes an open row so the hook must fire; completed rows must survive)

finding: idx_agent_task_list_workflow_run is a full btree over a mostly-NULL column; the sibling mcp_tool_calls.workflow_run_id uses a partial index (WHERE workflow_run_id IS NOT NULL).
fixed_in: FIX_ROUND-1 (index is now partial, matching the precedent)

finding: TOCTOU: a task row inserted by a still-live agent loop AFTER reconcile runs but under a now-terminal run leaks until the next boot sweep.
resolution: At a terminal transition the agent loop has returned (it is what produced the terminal outcome), so it does not create further task rows; the boot self-heal sweep is the documented backstop for any residual. Not worth a per-run lock/transaction for a low-severity race with a backstop.

finding: the chat agent-host path (ZIEE_CHAT_AGENT_CORE=1) creates task rows keyed by the assistant message id but never calls reconcile_run_terminal at stream-terminal; chat run_ids are absent from workflow_runs so neither the workflow writers nor the boot sweep heal them — no backstop.
resolution: DESCOPED per DEC-6: chat-agent-core is behind the non-default ZIEE_CHAT_AGENT_CORE flag (experimental), unmeasured by the rig, and outside the task's named scope (workflow runner + modules/agent). With the flag OFF (production default) the chat host is not used, so ZERO chat task rows exist and there is nothing to accumulate or leak. The run_id-keyed primitive already supports the message-id shape (proven by TEST-5), so the graduation fix is a known one-liner. DEC-6 strengthened to record the no-backstop caveat.

finding: chat/fan-out rows (workflow_run_id NULL, run_id has no FK) have no cascade cleanup or reconciliation path, so they could accumulate unbounded (§5).
resolution: Only reachable when ZIEE_CHAT_AGENT_CORE=1 (see the chat-gap finding). With the flag off (default) no chat/fan-out task rows are ever created, so there is nothing to accumulate. Tracked with the chat descope (DEC-6) for when the flag graduates.
